YOUR DREAM REMODELING

A remodel is one of the biggest investments you will ever make in your home, and the company behind it matters as much as the cabinets and countertops. Your Dream Remodeling is a full-service, design-build remodeling company based in Houston, Texas. Since 2010, we have helped homeowners across Greater Houston turn kitchen and bathroom ideas into finished rooms that look beautiful, work effortlessly, and hold up for years.

What makes us different is simple: the same company that designs your project also builds it. Design, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, tile, and countertops are handled by one accountable team, from the first sketch to the final walkthrough. No handoffs, no finger-pointing, no surprises halfway through your remodel.

Start with a free consultation. Call 281-550-8900 or request an appointment online.

Our Story: Built in Houston, Built on Design

Your Dream Remodeling started in 2010 with a frustration every homeowner knows: remodels that looked fine in a brochure but were never truly designed around the family living in them.

So we built the company the other way around. Design first, always. Before anyone talks about demolition, our design specialists sit with you and learn how your household actually lives: how you cook, clean, entertain, and get ready in the morning. Your must-have features, your routines, and your budget shape the plan, because in our process the most important factor is you.

That design-first approach carried us from a small Houston remodeling team to a company with its own Showroom and Design Center, where clients explore cabinet choices, fixtures, finishes, and full room displays in person. Today our team brings decades of combined professional experience in kitchen and bathroom design and construction to every project, whether it is a single cabinet installation or a complete spa-style master bathroom.

Kitchen Remodeling in Cypress, TX - Cabinets, Countertops, Islands and Custom Layouts

A kitchen remodel should make your home easier to live in, not simply newer to look at. Your Dream Remodeling provides kitchen remodeling in Cypress, TX for homeowners planning everything from cabinet and countertop upgrades to full kitchen renovations, new islands, open layouts and complete gut remodels. Cypress homes create very different remodeling decisions depending on where and when they were built. An established Fairfield or Coles Crossing kitchen may be reaching the point where the original cabinetry, lighting, tile and layout all need attention. A newer home in Bridgeland or Towne Lake may already have an open floor plan but still feel builder-standard rather than personal. Those projects should not receive the same remodeling plan. We begin by figuring out what is actually holding the kitchen back, then coordinate the layout, cabinetry, appliances, surfaces, lighting and construction scope around those priorities. Homeowners who want to understand our broader approach can also explore our kitchen remodeling services in Houston. Kitchen remodeling projects starting from $25,000

features.

Cypress Kitchen Remodeling Services

A successful Cypress kitchen remodeling project starts by defining the right level of work.

Kitchen Layout Redesign in Cypress

A beautiful kitchen can still be frustrating if circulation is wrong.

Before changing the footprint, we look at:

Refrigerator door swing
Dishwasher clearance
Oven and range access
Sink location
Pantry traffic
Island seating
Walkways
Drawer and cabinet clearance

One of the most common design problems is trying to force too much into the center of the room. An oversized island can look impressive on a rendering and become irritating when the dishwasher, refrigerator and bar stools compete for the same walkway. We design around movement first.

OPEN-CONCEPT REMODELING
Open-Concept Kitchen Remodeling in Cypress

If you are considering opening the kitchen further, the first question should not be what the new island looks like.

It should be what the wall is doing.

A wall may contain:

Structural framing
Electrical wiring
Plumbing
HVAC components
Switches and outlets
Flooring and ceiling transitions

If it is load-bearing, structural evaluation may be required before the final kitchen design is approved.

The cost of removing a wall can also include flooring, ceiling repair, lighting and cabinet redesign.

Ask About Opening Your Kitchen
CUSTOM CABINETRY
Custom Kitchen Cabinets in Cypress, TX

Full-height cabinetry
Should You Reface or Replace Your Cabinets?

Refacing can make sense when the existing cabinet boxes are solid, the kitchen layout works and the problem is primarily cosmetic. Replacement makes more sense when storage is poor, appliance locations are changing, cabinets are damaged or the kitchen needs a different footprint. Visit our kitchen design showroom to compare cabinet styles, finishes and material combinations.

Main household traffic

A successful island improves the kitchen when several people are using the room at once.

NEWER CYPRESS HOMES
Builder-Grade Kitchen Upgrades in Bridgeland, Towne Lake & Cypress Creek Lakes

A newer kitchen does not necessarily need a complete gut remodel. Sometimes the room is functionally sound but visually generic. In that situation, we first identify which parts of the original kitchen are worth preserving. Maybe the cabinet layout is good but storage needs improvement. Maybe the island is the right size but the countertop and lighting feel standard. Maybe the cabinets are acceptable but leave awkward unused space above. The goal is not to demolish good work for the sake of having a full remodel. For homeowners planning a Bridgeland kitchen remodel, Towne Lake remodel or kitchen renovation in Cypress Creek Lakes, this distinction can make the difference between a strategic upgrade and an unnecessarily expensive rebuild.

ESTABLISHED CYPRESS HOMES
Remodeling Established Kitchens in Fairfield, Coles Crossing & Longwood

Older Cypress communities often present a different set of decisions.

Common priorities can include:

Replacing aging cabinetry
Converting lower cabinets to drawers
Improving pantry storage
Updating lighting
Creating a larger island
Removing a peninsula
Opening the kitchen toward the living area
Replacing dated flooring
Planning for larger refrigerators or ranges

If the existing footprint works, keeping it can save significant money.

If it is the source of the kitchen’s problems, covering it with expensive new finishes simply locks those problems in.

PRE-CONSTRUCTION PLANNING
What Should Be Checked Before a Cypress Kitchen Remodel?

Good remodeling planning also means identifying conditions that can disrupt the design later.

Electrical Requirements

Modern appliances and lighting can change circuit requirements.

Plumbing

Range Hood Ventilation

Flooring

Structural Changes

PERMITS & HOA PLANNING
Cypress Remodeling Permits: What Homeowners Should Know

Cypress is not an incorporated city with its own municipal building department. Most Cypress properties are within unincorporated Harris County, so applicable residential permitting is handled through Harris County rather than a “City of Cypress” permit office. Exactly what approvals are required depends on the property and scope of work. Individual communities can also have deed restrictions or HOA architectural-review requirements. In master-planned areas such as Bridgeland, Towne Lake, Fairfield and Coles Crossing, homeowners should confirm whether the planned scope requires community approval in addition to any applicable county process. County permits and HOA approvals are separate considerations.

When homeowners compare kitchen remodelers in Cypress, TX, estimates can look similar until the details are examined.

Choosing a Remodeling Company in Cypress

Come to the showroom. Hold the tile, open vanity drawers, see quartz under real light.

Call 281-550-8900 during business hours and you’ll reach our office.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
How to Compare Bathroom Remodelers Near You

Get two or three quotes, and ask every company the same questions. The answers tell you more than the price does.

1.
Do you have a showroom I can visit?

A physical location means accountability.

2.
Is your crew in-house?

Or will the whole job be handed to a subcontractor you’ve never met?

3.
Who does the plumbing and electrical, and are they licensed in Texas?
4.
Who pulls permits?

The contractor should, not you.

5.
What waterproofing goes behind the shower tile?

You want a named system, like Schluter-KERDI, not “we use cement board.”

6.
Does the quote list every material?

Watch for large “allowances” that can grow later.

7.
How do you handle hidden damage?

It should be shown and priced before it’s fixed.

8.
What’s the warranty, and is there a deductible?
9.
Can I see local projects and real reviews?

Check Google and Houzz, not just the website.

Red flags to watch for
A large cash deposit before any design work
A price given over the phone without seeing the room
No written scope, or a one-line quote
Pressure to sign the same day
No physical address

BATHROOM REMODELING HOUSTON, TX
Bathroom Remodeling in Houston, TX

A bathroom remodel should do more than replace outdated tile. It should make the room easier to use, easier to maintain and better suited to the way you live today. Your Dream Remodeling provides full-service bathroom remodeling in Houston, TX, including complete bathroom renovations, master bathrooms, walk-in showers, tub-to-shower conversions, custom vanities, countertops, flooring and accessibility-focused upgrades. Start with a free in-home consultation, then explore cabinetry, fixtures, flooring and finishes at our Houston Showroom & Design Center at 1718 N Fry Rd, Suite 330, Houston, TX 77084.

or call 281-550-8900
YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Bathroom Remodeling Designed Around How You Use the Space

Most homeowners are not remodeling simply because they want different tile. Usually, the shower feels cramped, the tub is rarely used, storage is limited, lighting is poor or the original layout wastes valuable floor space.

A successful bathroom renovation starts with layout, storage, shower size, accessibility and existing conditions before moving into materials and finishes.

For a broader look at the renovation options we provide, explore our remodeling services.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Bathroom Remodeling Services in Houston
01
Complete Bathroom Remodels

A complete bathroom renovation may include demolition, shower or bathtub replacement, plumbing and electrical updates, waterproofing, tile, cabinetry, vanity countertops, flooring, lighting, shower glass and finishing work.

Planning the entire room as one project allows the layout, materials and construction details to work together instead of becoming disconnected upgrades.

02
Master Bathroom Remodeling

Primary bathrooms often provide the biggest opportunity to improve comfort and functionality.

Common upgrades include:

Larger walk-in showers
Freestanding tubs
Double vanities
Better drawer and linen storage
Frameless shower glass
New flooring
Improved lighting

A larger bathroom does not always need more fixtures. Removing an unused element can sometimes create better circulation, more storage or a more comfortable shower.

Planning a larger primary suite? Explore our Master Bathroom Remodel Guide for more detail on layouts, materials and design decisions.

03
Walk-In Shower Remodeling

A properly planned walk-in shower can improve both accessibility and everyday use.

Options may include built-in niches, bench seating, handheld shower fixtures, frameless glass, low-threshold or curbless entry, updated drainage and waterproofing.

For shower styles, conversions and planning considerations, visit our Walk-In Shower Guide.

04
Tub-to-Shower Conversions

If a bathtub is rarely used, converting its footprint into a shower can provide a wider entrance, more usable shower space and easier everyday access.

Before removing a tub, consider the home’s other bathrooms, who uses the space and your long-term plans. The right decision should be based on how the room is actually used.

05
Guest, Small Bathroom and Powder Room Remodeling

Compact bathrooms benefit from careful planning. Better-scaled vanities, improved lighting, practical storage, easy-care surfaces and a more efficient shower or tub layout can make limited square footage work harder.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Bathroom Cabinets, Tile and Countertops

Bathroom materials should be selected for durability, maintenance and design compatibility.

Cabinetry may include stock, semi-custom or custom vanities, with storage options such as drawer stacks, linen towers and medicine cabinets.

Porcelain tile is a practical option for floors and shower walls because of its low water absorption and broad range of finishes.

Natural stone can create a distinctive appearance but generally requires more maintenance.

Quartz countertops provide a nonporous, low-maintenance vanity surface with many colors and patterns available.

Shower glass may be frameless, framed or sliding depending on the layout, door clearance and budget.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Layout Changes, Lighting and Ventilation

Keeping major fixtures close to existing plumbing locations can help control remodeling costs. However, changing the layout can be worthwhile when the existing footprint is the main problem.

That may include enlarging a shower, removing a garden tub, moving a vanity, improving door clearance or opening a partition.

Lighting and ventilation should also be considered early. Vanity lighting, ceiling lighting, wet-location fixtures and appropriate ventilation all affect how the finished bathroom performs.

Where required, plumbing, electrical and mechanical work is handled through appropriately licensed Texas specialty contractors.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Accessibility and Aging-in-Place Remodeling

Accessibility-focused bathroom design can improve safety without making the room feel institutional.

Options may include:

Curbless or low-threshold showers
Wider shower entrances
Shower benches
Handheld shower heads
Grab bars
Slip-resistant flooring
Comfort-height toilets
Walk-in tubs

Curbless showers require careful planning of floor slope, drainage and waterproofing.

Homeowners considering accessible bathing can also explore our Houston Walk-In Tub Guide.

A clear proposal should explain what is included and how unforeseen work or change orders are handled.

Project duration depends on scope, material lead times and existing conditions.

A small same-footprint guest bathroom should not follow the same schedule as a master bathroom involving plumbing relocation, custom cabinetry, countertops and a new shower.

Bathroom remodeling typically moves through preparation, demolition, wet-area work, cabinetry, countertops, flooring, wall finishes, shower glass and final completion.

Bathroom Remodeling Permits in Houston

Permit requirements depend on the scope of work and the property’s jurisdiction.

Finish-only work may not require the same permits as projects involving plumbing, electrical or structural changes. Applicable trade work should be handled by appropriately licensed contractors.

Permit requirements should therefore be reviewed against the actual project rather than assuming every bathroom renovation follows the same rules.

YOUR DREAM REMODELING
Why Katy Bathrooms Wear Out the Way They Do

Katy grew fast. Whole neighborhoods went up in a few years, often with the same builder packages repeated street after street. That means Katy bathrooms tend to fail in predictable ways. Knowing them upfront helps you plan the right remodel, not just a prettier version of the same problem.

01
The oversized tub and the undersized shower

Builders in the late ‘90s and 2000s loved the garden tub. Homeowners today mostly don’t. Removing the tub and combining both spaces into one walk-in shower usually gives you a shower that’s two or three times bigger, with room for a bench, a niche and a real glass enclosure. Worried about losing the tub? As long as the house keeps one tub, usually in a hall or kids’ bath, most Katy buyers won’t miss it in the master.

02
Floor tile that keeps cracking

Katy homes sit on slab foundations over expansive clay. The clay swells after heavy rain and shrinks through long, dry summers, and the slab moves a little with it. Tile set straight onto concrete doesn’t forgive that movement. You’ll see it as hairline cracks running across several tiles or grout that keeps popping loose. We fix the cause. New floors go down over an uncoupling membrane like Schluter-DITRA, and we place movement joints where the tile industry standards call for them. As members of the National Tile Contractors Association, that’s how we’re trained to set tile on a slab that moves.

03
White crust on glass and chrome

Soft walls behind the old shower
